_comment: DBE Grade 12 Accounting P2, November 2025. Questions + marking-guideline
answers extracted from the text layer of the PDFs in this directory
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and cross-checked by recomputing figures.
Schema follows past_papers/accounting/grade12/2024/paper1.json. The
optional 'information' field (array of verbatim lines) carries the
INFORMATION / pre-adjustment data block of each question section; it is
attached to the FIRST sub-question of that section and applies to all
sub-questions of the same section.
Sub-parts that the paper prints as unnumbered bullets are given suffixed
refs (e.g. Q1.2.2a, Q4.2.2b) in printed order.
The pre-printed SPECIAL ANSWER BOOK (paper2_answer_book.pdf) is also
tracked in this directory; where the memo references the ANSWER BOOK,
the pre-printed figures/format are described in the relevant question's
text or memo_working.
memo_working reproduces the marking guideline's figures and allocation
notation (one mark / two marks / one part correct / operation / method
mark). The memo's tick glyphs are images and did not survive text
extraction; their per-figure placement is therefore described in words,
not drawn.
The paper's instruction table: Q1 Reconciliations 40 marks 30 min;
Q2 Stock Valuation 35 marks 30 min; Q3 Cost Accounting 35 marks 30 min;
Q4 Budgeting and Problem-solving 40 marks 30 min. A Financial Indicator
Formula Sheet is attached to the paper (standard NSC sheet, not
transcribed here).
Anomaly 1: the paper's Q4.1 Information C states 'All assistants will
receive a 60% bonus in December 2026', although the budget period ends
31 January 2026 and the Projected Statement of Comprehensive Income
extract covers Dec. 2025; the memo applies the 60% bonus to the
December 2025 salaries (primary answer 128 000 = 80 000 + 48 000) but
also prints an alternative answer of 80 000 (one method mark). The paper
wording appears to be a misprint for December 2025.
Anomaly 2: memo 2.2.3 quotes a Rotrim stockholding period of 124,7 days;
this could not be reproduced from the given figures (closing-stock basis
635 500 / 1 224 500 x 365 = 189,4 days; average-stock basis = 164,0
days). The Punchies (127,8 days) and Clear View (23,1 days over the
5 months since introduction) figures do recompute.

questions.text: BANK RECONCILIATION: The information relates to Duma Stores on 31 July 2025. The business is owned by Duma Mathupha. They use the official Bank Statement, received on the 28th of each month, to reconcile their Cash Journals. Complete the table provided in the ANSWER BOOK by showing the entries that must be recorded in the Cash Journals on 31 July 2025. (The ANSWER BOOK pre-prints a two-column table headed Cash Receipts Journal R162 000 and Cash Payments Journal R55 200.)
questions.memo_working: CRJ: 2 160 (two marks) is the correction of EFT 124 (recorded as R5 310 in June, correct on the Bank Statement at R3 150); 16 500 (one mark) + 16 500 (one mark) = 33 000 corrects the tenant Q Ngcobo direct deposit that was recorded in the CPJ (cancel the CPJ entry and record the receipt). CPJ: 10 000 (two marks) missing cash on the 30 June deposit (R18 600 cash slips vs R8 600 banked, irrecoverable); 2 700 (one mark) + 2 700 (one mark) = 5 400 for the Prime Insurers debit orders (June and July); 13 000 (one mark) debit card payment to Star Motors; 975 (one mark) interest; 605 (one mark) service fees. -1 foreign (max -1) (only if marks are scored elsewhere for the same figure); -1 superfluous items (max -1); ensure that the candidate does not get full marks for including any incorrect figure/s.
information: A. Extract from the Bank Reconciliation Statement on 30 June 2025:
Outstanding deposits: Dated 29 June 2025, R132 000; Dated 30 June 2025, R18 600
Outstanding EFTs: EFT 124 (Typek Stationers), R5 310; EFT 125 (Cola Stores), R9 990
B. Provisional totals in the Cash Journals on 31 July 2025 before receiving the Bank Statement:
Cash Receipts Journal R162 000 | Cash Payments Journal R55 200
C. Items on the Bank Statement that do not agree with July 2025 Cash Journals:
(i) The internal auditor discovered that the supporting cash slips for the deposit on 30 June 2025 amounted to R18 600. The shortfall is irrecoverable because the cashier at that time has resigned.
(ii) EFT 124 on 3 July 2025 (Typek Stationers) is correct on the Bank Statement.
(iii) The direct deposit on 10 July 2025 by Q Ngcobo (a tenant) was recorded incorrectly in the Cash Payments Journal.

(iv) The debit order on 15 July 2025 to Prime Insurers for the business insurance was processed twice due to insufficient funds in June. The amounts covered payments for both June and July 2025 to bring the account up to date.
(v) A bank transfer on 28 July 2025 in favour of A-Z Suppliers was overstated by R11 000 by the bank clerk. The bank was notified and will correct the error in August 2025.
D. Entries in the Cash Journals for July 2025 that were not reflected on the July 2025 Bank Statement:
Deposit on 30 July 2025: R41 850; EFT 207: R7 650; EFT 208: R10 800

E. Duma, the owner, used a business debit card on 29 July 2025 for the payment of R13 000 to Star Motors for repairs to the company vehicle, but he neglected to submit the transaction slip to the bookkeeper.
F. The Bank Statement on 28 July 2025 showed a favourable balance of R119 080.

questions.text: Prepare the Bank Reconciliation Statement on 31 July 2025. (The ANSWER BOOK offers a choice of two templates: a two-column method with Debit and Credit columns, OR a one-column method. Choose only ONE.)
questions.memo_answer: Balance as per Bank Statement 119 080 (favourable); Outstanding deposit 41 850; Outstanding EFTs: No. 207 (7 650), No. 208 (10 800); Incorrect EFT +11 000; Debit card on 29 July 2025 (13 000); Balance as per bank account 140 480 (favourable)
questions.memo_working: Two-column method: Credit side: Balance as per Bank Statement 119 080 (one mark); Outstanding deposit 41 850 (one mark); Incorrect EFT 11 000 (one mark); total 171 930. Debit side: Outstanding EFT No. 207 7 650 (one mark); No. 208 10 800 (one mark); Debit card on 29 July 2025 13 000 (one mark); Balance as per bank account 140 480 (one method mark, could be Cr); totals 171 930 both sides (DR and CR totals must be the same). One-column method: 119 080 + 41 850 - 7 650 - 10 800 + 11 000 - 13 000 = 140 480 (same mark allocation; candidates must present the appropriate sign, positive or negative; be alert to candidates who start with the bank account balance or vice versa). -1 presentation (max -1) (inappropriate/no details); -1 for foreign items (max -2) if marks awarded elsewhere. For the two-column method, candidates must place figures in the correct column to earn marks. In awarding the method mark for the balancing bank account figure, ensure that candidates do not get full marks for including any incorrect figure/s.

questions.text: Identify TWO problems (with figures) with the management of cash in Duma Stores. In EACH case, provide a different solution for how these problems can be prevented in future.
questions.topic: Bank Reconciliation - Internal Control over Cash
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO problems with figures (2 marks each pair) plus a different solution for each (1 mark each): Missing cash of R10 000 - outsource the collection of cash by security companies / encourage EFT or card payments by customers / implement dual authorisation for cash deposits / separation of duties / conduct unannounced cash counts or surprise check / request bank notification. Incorrect recording of transactions in Cash Journals, R16 500/R5 310 - double check the recording of financial transactions / daily cash reconciliation. Poor budgeting for debit orders / cash flow problems / unpaid debit order, R2 700 - keep sufficient cash to pay debit orders / automate alerts and reminders for debit orders. questions.text: CREDITORS' RECONCILIATION: PG Stores is owned by Portia Gina and she buys goods on credit from Matsulu Suppliers. The statement of account received from Matsulu Suppliers reflected a balance of R287 600 for June 2025. Use the table in the ANSWER BOOK to indicate how the relevant balances will change when preparing the Creditors' Reconciliation. Indicate the amount, as well as a (+) for increase and a (-) for decrease. (The ANSWER BOOK pre-prints a table with rows (i) to (vi) and the incorrect balances: Creditors' Ledger Account of Matsulu Suppliers 270 140 | Statement of Account 287 600.)
questions.memo_answer: Creditors' Ledger Account of Matsulu Suppliers: balance 270 140; (i) -3 600; (iii) -32 400; (iv) +1 410; total 235 550. Statement of Account: balance 287 600; (ii) +60 000; (iv) +330; (v) +42 000; (vi) -154 380; total 235 550
questions.memo_working: (i) [-17 280 + 13 680] = -3 600 (two marks) in the Creditors' Ledger (Debit Note 785 recorded at 13 680 instead of 17 280). (ii) [100 500 - 40 500] = +60 000 (two marks) on the statement (Invoice 471 recorded as 40 500). (iii) -16 200 (one mark) - 16 200 (one mark) = -32 400 in the Creditors' Ledger (the 24 June merchandise return was entered in the credit column instead of the debit column). (iv) +1 410 (one mark) in the Creditors' Ledger (interest not yet recorded); +330 (one mark) on the statement (interest 1 080 corrected to 1 410). (v) +42 000 (one mark) on the statement (Invoice 681 of 28 June; the statement reflects transactions up to 25 June only). (vi) -154 380 (one mark) on the statement (EFT and discount of 29 June). Totals 235 550 both columns (one part correct for both totals; must include opening balances; could be different amounts). Accept brackets for negative sign; if no sign assume positive. Accept correct identifiable amounts presented in wrong line/s. Foreign entries: -1 per line if a mark has been scored on that line.
information: A. Creditors' Ledger Account of PG Stores: Creditors' Ledger of PG Stores - Matsulu Suppliers
B. When comparing the Creditors' Ledger to the statement of account received from Matsulu Suppliers, the following differences were noted:
(i) Debit Note 785 was incorrectly recorded in the Creditors' Ledger. The statement shows the correct amount of R17 280.
(ii) Invoice 471 was incorrectly recorded on the statement from Matsulu Suppliers as R40 500.
(iii) The transaction on 24 June 2025 in the Creditors' Ledger is for merchandise returned to Matsulu Suppliers.
(iv) The statement showed interest charged at R1 080. The correct amount of interest is R1 410. No entry was made into the Creditors' Ledger.
(v) The statement reflects transactions up to 25 June 2025.
(vi) All other transactions recorded in the Creditors' Ledger appeared correctly in the statement of account received from Matsulu Suppliers.

questions.text: The purchasing manager of PG Stores ordered six chairs for the offices. His friend, Mike, the sales manager of Comfy Suppliers, invoiced PG Stores at R30 000 per chair on the purchasing manager's request. The internal auditor has discovered that the chairs are trading at an actual price of R7 500 each. Explain how the business can prevent this problem from happening in the future, excluding separation of duties. Provide TWO points.
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO valid points (do not accept separation of duties): Orders and payment to be authorised by senior personnel; Establishment of procurement committee / obtain multiple quotations per order to enhance the procurement process / ensure supplier reliability and fair pricing through a proper vetting process; Regularly compare competitor prices using updated catalogues; Conduct frequent audits of purchasing transactions; Employees must disclose personal ties with suppliers to avoid biasness.

questions.text: What action should be taken against the purchasing manager, besides dismissing him? Provide ONE point.
questions.memo_answer: Any ONE valid point (do not accept dismiss the purchasing manager): Disciplinary hearing / verbal or written warning / temporary suspension / lay charges against him; Recover the excess amount added during the purchase of chairs / deduct money from his salary to recover financial loss; Reassign the purchasing manager to a different section or department / demote him to another department; Limit the purchasing manager's contact with suppliers to prevent misconduct; Blacklist the purchasing manager from future employment of similar position.

questions.text: SUPERSAVERS SUPERMARKET: The information relates to flavoured juices (2-litre bottles) that Supersavers Supermarket trades with. The first-in-first-out (FIFO) stock valuation method is applicable. The business is managed by Bryan Mills. The financial year ended on 28 February 2025. Calculate the value of the closing stock on 28 February 2025, using the FIFO method.
questions.memo_answer: R40 350 (one part correct; both amounts added)
questions.memo_working: (818 x 42) = 34 356 (three marks) [818 = 850 - 32 returns] + (162 x 37) = 5 994 (two method marks + one mark) [162 = 980 - 818 OR 150 + 12] = 40 350. For the two method marks both quantities must add up to 980. OR (35 700 - 1 344) (one mark + two marks) + (5 550 + 444) (one mark + two method marks). Ensure that only one option is marked consistently.

B. Purchases and returns during the year: (columns: NUMBER OF UNITS | UNIT PRICE (R) | TOTAL (R))
C. Sales: 10 118 units were sold at R47 per bottle: R475 546

questions.text: Bryan has noticed that some of the stock of flavoured juices has exceeded their shelf life (sell-by date) of 65 days. Identify the value of stock that Bryan is referring to, using the FIFO stock valuation method.
questions.memo_answer: 444 (one part correct)
questions.memo_working: 12 x 37 OR 96 200 - 95 756 OR 5 994 - 5 550 = 444 (the 12 December 2024 units still on hand are older than 65 days at year-end).

questions.text: How can Bryan manage the stock of flavoured juices to avoid losses incurred by the business? Provide TWO points.
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO relevant points (2 marks each): Purchase stock more frequently instead of buying in bulk; Identify old stock close to expiry date and offer it to customers at a reduced price / use inventory software to monitor sales and expiry dates of stock / perform routine inventory checks regularly to reconcile records; Train employees to understand proper rotation of stock / arrange stock in the supermarket to position new stock correctly.

questions.text: Punchies model: Calculate the stockholding period (in days) using the closing stock.
questions.memo_answer: 127,8 days (one part correct; must x 365; days not necessary; accept 128 days / 127 days)

questions.text: Comment on the stockholding period. Provide ONE point, with figures. The stockholding period for the year ended 30 June 2024 was 69 days.
questions.memo_answer: Comparison with figures (1 mark); comment (1 mark): It has increased (from 69 days) to 127,8 days (see 2.2.2) / by 58,8 days. Other printer models may become outdated due to an improved technology on Clear View printer / stock moving slow (piling) due to delayed sales / there will be increased storage costs decreasing profitability / increased risk of printers being stolen / cash tied up in stock instead of being available for other expenses.

questions.text: Clear View model: Although the Clear View model had units returned, Moses is very pleased with his decision to introduce it as a new model. Provide TWO points (with figures) to explain why Moses is pleased.
questions.memo_answer: Compare Clear View printer with other printers (2 marks); figures (2 marks). Any TWO of: Each printer is sold at a profit of R14 000 (total gross profit R910 000), higher than that of the other two printers; Sold an average of 13 printers per month, surpassing Rotrim (7) and Punchies (8); Sold 86,7% of available printers, compared to (65,8%) of Rotrim or (74,1%) of Punchies / sold 65 units in 5 months, compared to Rotrim (79 units) and Punchies (100 units) over 12 months; Achieved the highest sales of R3 185 000, exceeding Rotrim (R1 714 300) and Punchies (R3 108 000); Only 10 (R350 000) units left, compared to (41 units) (R780 500) for Rotrim and (35 units) (R635 500) for Punchies; Stockholding period is only 23,1 days compared to (127,8 days) of Punchies and (124,7 days) of Rotrim.
questions.memo_note: The memo's Rotrim stockholding figure of 124,7 days could not be reproduced from the given data (closing-stock basis gives 189,4 days); its bullet also attaches 780 500/41 units to Rotrim and 635 500/35 units to Punchies, the reverse of the values computed in 2.2.1 and 2.2.2a. Both appear to be memo slips; transcribed verbatim.

questions.text: Moses wants to reduce the number of units being returned to the suppliers. Give ONE suggestion on how this can be achieved.
questions.memo_answer: Any relevant suggestion: Ensure that the printer is in working condition when it is bought; Change supplier to boost reliability and customer satisfaction of Clear View; Request guarantee / warranty terms from suppliers; Train staff on handling procedures / store printers correctly to prevent damages.

questions.text: VIVAN TRADERS: Information is provided for the budget period ending 31 January 2026. Complete the Debtors' Collection Schedule for January 2026. questions.text: WARMBAD TRADERS: The business sells gas stoves and the information relates to the period September and October 2025. Dozer Moyo, the manager, is impressed with the performance of Warmbad Traders. The business has consistently outperformed its only competitor in the area, Woodlands Traders, due to a bigger client base and being competitive. Woodlands Traders decided to close their business in September 2025. As a result, Warmbad Traders became the only gas stove supplier in the area. Explain why it is important to compare the budgeted figures with the actual figures. Provide ONE point.
questions.memo_answer: Any valid point: To check if the budget is realistic / it helps to refine and create more realistic future budgets; Detecting variance on receipts and payments; Anticipate how the bank balance will be affected; Assessing how well the business achieved its financial targets; To encourage responsible financial behaviour by monitoring how funds are used / ensures spending and income are managed within limits and prevents overspending.
information: A. Extract from the Cash Budget:

questions.text: Loss of sales: The number of units sold in October has decreased. Give a reason, with figures, for this decrease.

questions.memo_answer: 156 240 (one part correct)

questions.text: State TWO benefits that Warmbad Traders will forfeit by failing to meet its financial obligations with suppliers in October 2025.
questions.memo_answer: Any TWO valid points: Forfeit the early repayment discount; Lose advantage of trade discounts for loyal customers / forfeit bulk-buying discounts and priority deals; Credit score or rating will decrease which will affect future credit applications / reputation of the business will be tarnished; Future credit limit will be affected; Suppliers might switch to a cash-only policy, affecting the business's cash flow.

questions.text: Remuneration to employees: Give ONE reason for Dozer awarding his employees with commission during September 2025. Quote figures.
questions.memo_answer: Any ONE valid point (1 mark) with figure/s (1 mark): Number of units sold increased (from 90) to 124 / by 34 / by 37,8%; Sales increased by R54 400 (34 x R1 600) / by 37,8%; Cash surplus increased (from R63 800) to R98 950 / by 55,1%.

questions.text: Give ONE reason why the employees will not be satisfied with the revised remuneration policy. Quote figures.
questions.memo_answer: Any ONE valid point (with figures): Total earnings for October R31 500 (R10 500 per employee) is lower than September salaries of R38 400 (R12 800 per employee) / by R6 900 (by R2 300 per employee) / by 18%; Total salaries and commission in September of R42 300 is more than total salaries and commission in October of R31 500 / by R10 800 (R3 600 per employee).
